key_idea: Since moves are only S/W/E without revisits, a path never reverses direction inside a row, so the state (cell, last move direction, trie node of the word in progress) is enough and plain BFS gives the shortest path.
sketch: Build a trie of the words (at most 2501 nodes). BFS over states (cell, dir in {came south, moving west, moving east}, trie node): from a west-moving state you may go west or south, from east-moving east or south, after a south step anything. On stepping to a letter go to the child of the current node, and if the current node ends a word also to the child of the root. Start from every top-row cell matching a root child with distance 1; stop at the first popped state in the bottom row whose node is terminal. At most 2500*3*2501 = 18.8M states with 16-bit distances; O(states * 6). Pitfalls: grid letters are space separated, m=1 is allowed, the path may walk along the bottom row before ending.
